S12.5 done: `assertEmptyOpclassIndexStillBlocksSorts` fired as designed and is now `assertHostedPGCanSort`, with `0130-0002` Guard #1 restored to its `ORDER BY c.relname` form. S12.3/S12.4 resolved as NON-actions: the placeholder lists are the sibling-correct pattern (2687/2754/2755 all stay listed and are overwritten by their bootstrapper), and 2687 was already bulk-loaded. Incidental fix: 2754 passed `nkeyatts = 4` for a 3-key index and is multi-leaf, so the wrong `indnkeyatts` was baked into its pivot tuples. Gates: the S4 E2E PASS (24 s), `internal/initdb` PASS (63 s), `^TestE2E_` family PASS (100 s), UNITS + pgbench smoke via the hook. **Follow-ups ledgered:** initdb-time only (existing bench clusters need re-initdb), cross-type `pg_amop` heap rows still out of scope, and a NEW finding — an assert-enabled hosted PG traps in `procarray.c:2857` `TransactionIdIsNormal(latestCompletedXid)` from the bgwriter ~15 s in, which no current E2E runs long enough to see. **NOTE — id collision:** a SECOND, unrelated item below also carries the id `M0131-S12` (goopg stamps `DB_IN_PRODUCTION`, design `0131-0014`); it is untouched by this loop and needs renumbering. (orig est ~1 loop; MEASURED by M0131-S4 F1). A real PG hosted on a goopg directory cannot execute **any** sort, for **any** type: `SELECT x FROM (VALUES (2), (1)) v(x) ORDER BY x` fails *"could not identify an ordering operator for type integer"*. `lookup_type_cache(TYPECACHE_LT_OPR)` → `GetDefaultOpClass` scans `pg_opclass` through `OpclassAmNameNspIndexId` (**2686**) with `indexOK = true` and NO seq-scan fallback (`postgres/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c:2374-2384`) — the same shape as blockers #7/#8 and M0131-S5. The heap is correct (probed on the hosted PG: 177 rows; `int4_ops` = oid 1978, `opcmethod` 403, `opcdefault` 't'; 38 default btree opclasses) and `pg_index` carries valid 2686/2687 rows; the index is EMPTY. `internal/initdb/initdb.go` writes 2686 as a bare `makeBtreeRootPage()` placeholder (three lists, ~:1902/:2047/:2144) while its sibling `pg_opfamily_am_name_nsp_index` (2754) has a real bulk-load bootstrapper, and `pgBuildIndexTupleOidNameOidKey` (`internal/initdb/btree_index_bootstrap.go:1909`) **already names 2686 in its doc comment** as one of the two indexes it serves — no caller ever builds its tuples. Subtasks: S12.1 add a `bootstrapPgOpclassAmNameNspIndex` on the 2754 bootstrapper's exact pattern (`btree_index_bootstrap.go:1972-2021`), keyed `(opcmethod oid_ops, opcname name_ops, opcnamespace oid_ops)` UNIQUE per `pgIndexInitialEntries` at `internal/initdb/initdb.go:4934`; S12.2 write it into `base/1` AND `base/5` like every sibling; S12.3 remove 2686 from the three empty-root-page lists; S12.4 check 2687 (`pg_opclass_oid_index`) for the same gap — it sits in the same lists and PG's `RelationCacheInitializePhase3` may nail it; S12.5 INVERT `assertEmptyOpclassIndexStillBlocksSorts` in `internal/testport/e2e_pg_coldstart_on_goopgdata_test.go`, restore the `ORDER BY` form of the Guard-#1 query and drop the Go-side sort. **Scope limit to ledger: initdb-time only** — every existing goopg `$PGDATA` (bench clusters 65433/65436/65437, any operator dir) keeps the empty index, re-initdb required.
- [x] **M0131-S13 — `pg_proc.proconfig` must be NULL, not a malformed array** (DONE 2026-08-12) (est ~1-2 loops; MEASURED by M0131-S4 F2). Calling ANY non-builtin function on a hosted PG aborts the backend: `SELECT 'a'::text || 1` gives `TRAP: failed Assert("ARR_NDIM(array) == 1"), File: "guc.c", Line: 6411` via `TransformGUCArray` ← `fmgr_security_definer` ← `client backend was terminated by signal 6`. goopg writes **all 3397** `pg_proc` rows with a non-NULL `proconfig` (probed: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proconfig IS NOT NULL` = 3397 = the full row count; `prosecdef` is correctly `'f'` everywhere, so it is `proconfig` alone) and the bytes are not a valid 1-D `text[]`. Upstream's trigger is `fmgr_info_cxt_security` (`postgres/src/backend/utils/fmgr/fmgr.c:203-211`): `prosecdef || !heap_attisnull(…, Anum_pg_proc_proconfig, NULL) || FmgrHookIsNeeded`. Blast radius is bounded by `fmgr_isbuiltin` — an OID in the compiled-in `fmgrtab` never reads `pg_proc`, so `int4eq`/`textout`/`count`/`sum` are fine; the LANGUAGE SQL builtins break, `textanycat` (2003) among them. This is an assert-enabled PG build so the failure is loud; a production build would walk a bogus `ArrayType`, which is worse. Subtasks: S13.1 find where the pg_proc heap tuple's null bitmap is built (`internal/initdb/pg_proc_seed_data.go` + its tuple encoder) and determine whether the bug is a short bitmap, a wrong `t_hoff`, or a written-empty-varlena; S13.2 **check the trailing attributes as a group** — `proconfig`, `proacl`, `prosqlbody`, `probin` are all nullable and adjacent, so a single bitmap error hits several, and the sibling-paths rule applies; S13.3 the sharper related fact from F3 — `attmissingval` is not a column in goopg's `pg_attribute` self-description, i.e. the trailing-nullable-attribute handling may be systematically short across catalogs, so probe `pg_class`/`pg_attribute`/`pg_type` the same way rather than fixing `pg_proc` alone; S13.4 INVERT `assertProconfigGapStillCrashesSQLFunctions` and fold `label || '/' || qty` back into the row-content reads. **RESOLVED 2026-08-12.** Root cause was a STALE SIBLING, not a bitmap/`t_hoff` defect as S13.1 hypothesised: goopg has two builders for the 30-column physical `pg_proc` row and only one was right. The runtime `buildPGProcRow` (`internal/executor/sys_pg_proc.go`) already wrote `executor.NullDatum` for every absent nullable varlena, with a comment saying exactly why; the initdb seed builder `pgProcRow` (`internal/initdb/initdb.go`) wrote `NewStringDatum("")`, which falls through `encodeValuePG` to `emptyArrayTypeBytes` — a NON-NULL zero-dimension `ArrayType`. `NullBitmapPG`/`writeMultiPageHeapRows` were already correct and unchanged; they simply had nothing to mark. Fixed for the whole trailing nullable group per S13.2 (`proallargtypes`, `proargmodes`, `proargnames`, `proargdefaults` when `pronargdefaults=0`, `protrftypes`, `probin`, `prosqlbody`, `proconfig`, `proacl`) — fixing `proconfig` alone would have left `prosqlbody` as an empty `pg_node_tree`, i.e. `stringToNode("")`, one probe away. **Measured on a real hosted PG:** `SELECT 'a'::text || 1` = `a1` and `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proconfig IS NOT NULL` = **0** (was 3397). Guard `internal/initdb/pg_proc_nullable_varlena_test.go` sweeps all 3397 seed entries at the `Row` level AND re-decodes a physical tuple through `DecodeRowIntoMctxPGTuple` (the `Row` half alone passes even if the tuple writer drops the bitmap); proven fail-when-broken (restore `NewStringDatum("")` on proconfig → fails at `oid=3 heap_tableam_handler`). S13.4 done: `assertProconfigGapStillCrashesSQLFunctions` INVERTED to `assertHostedPGCanCallSQLBuiltins` (success + the zero-count, since either alone passes vacuously), `label || '/' || qty` folded back into the row-content reads as the new tripwire, and the probe is no longer destructive so it runs inline before guard 4. **S13.3 half-discharged:** `pg_attribute` was already correct (Step 3u fixed the identical bug); `pg_class`'s `pgClassNailedRow` still writes `relacl='{}'`/`reloptions='{}'`/`relpartbound=''` where upstream leaves NULL — LATENT (the E2E connects as superuser, who bypasses `pg_class_aclcheck`), so ledgered 2026-08-12 with a non-superuser probe as the resume point rather than fixed blind. Design: `0131-0004` §Findings F2.
- [x] **M0131-S14 — Fast defaults: `atthasmissing`/`attmissingval` (DONE 2026-08-12; a real PG 18.3 cold-started on a goopg directory now materialises an `ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT` value on pre-existing short tuples through its own `getmissingattr()`. S14.3 remains DEFERRED and ledgered — see the end of this item. MEASURED by M0131-S4 F3).** `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN tag text DEFAULT 'dflt'` reads back `'dflt'` on goopg and **NULL on the hosted PG** for all 15 pre-existing rows. The `pg_attrdef` half is CORRECT and is asserted positively by the test (the hosted PG reads `pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid)` = `'dflt'::text` on `adnum` 4, `relnatts` = 4) — that is M0130's 2604/2656/2657 work validated outside the basebackup lane for the first time. Missing is PG's fast-default mechanism: since PG 11 an ADD COLUMN with a non-volatile DEFAULT does not rewrite the heap; it stores the value in `pg_attribute.attmissingval` with `atthasmissing = true` and short tuples materialise it on read. goopg does neither. **S14.1 DONE 2026-08-12** — the prerequisite is discharged. The 42703 was NOT a missing heap row (relid 1249 always had 25, `attmissingval` among them) but `pg_class.relnatts = 24` on the nailed row: PG unlinks goopg's `pg_internal.init` at startup (`xlog.c:5633`) and builds `pg_attribute` from its own compiled 25-column `Desc_pg_attribute`, then `RelationCacheInitializePhase3` copies `rd_rel` out of goopg's `pg_class` tuple, and the short `relnatts` truncated the last column — which in PG18 order is `attmissingval`. Fixing it exposed a permutation: goopg's tail was `attacl/attoptions/attfdwoptions/attmissingval/attstattarget`, PG18's is `attstattarget/attacl/attoptions/attfdwoptions/attmissingval` (`attstattarget` moved to #21 when it became nullable; the code's comment still claimed #4, PG16's position). Invisible while all five are NULL — same null bitmap, same `t_hoff` — but `SET STATISTICS` writes `attstattarget` and a hosted PG read it as `attacl`. Four sibling definitions had drifted; `initdb.pgAttributeAttrs` (a 24-column PG-11-era layout with an `attcacheoff` PG18 removed) now derives from `pgAttrColDefs`, and the other two are pinned by `TestPGAttributeSelfDescriptionIsPG18Canonical` / `TestPGAttributeColumnsPG18IsCanonical`. Verified on a hosted PG: `attmissingval` reads, `relnatts`=25, tail attnums PG18-ordered. Ledger row 2026-08-12 M0131-S14.1 carries the two remaining type-fidelity divergences (`attoptions`/`attfdwoptions` declared `text` not `text[]`, `attmissingval` `text` not `anyarray`; `attstattarget` derived NOT NULL) — both inert until S14.2 puts a real value in the group. **S14.2 + S14.4 DONE 2026-08-12** — `buildUserPGAttributeRow` now writes `atthasmissing` plus the one-element `ArrayType` that `StoreAttrMissingVal` (`postgres/src/backend/catalog/heap.c:2030`) builds via `construct_array`: `ndim=1`, `dataoffset=0` (a NULL default stores nothing — `ATExecAddColumn` skips the call when `missingIsNull`), `elemtype` = the COLUMN's own `atttypid`, `dims[0]=lbound[0]=1`, element normalised to the 4-byte varlena header. The value itself still comes from the existing fast-default backfill (`catalog.Column.MissingValue`); an encode failure degrades to the pre-S14.2 shape rather than failing the DDL. **Two sibling divergences had to be fixed WITH it, exactly as the S14.1 ledger row predicted:** `attmissingval` was declared `text` in all three column lists where PG has `anyarray` (2277) — PG dereferences the datum as `ArrayType *` — and `anyarray` carries `typalign => 'd'` (`postgres/src/include/catalog/pg_type.dat:573`), 8 bytes, not the `'i'` every other varlena array uses; both `initdb.pgTypeAlignChar` and `executor.physicalPGTypeAlign` had grouped it with the 4-byte varlenas, which also under-padded `pg_statistic.stavalues1..5`. Same shape as S14.1 and S13 for the fourth/fifth time this milestone: an always-NULL column hides sibling disagreement until something writes it. Measured on the hosted PG: `atthasmissing='t'` for `s4_items.tag` and `tag='dflt'` on all 15 physically short pre-ALTER rows, with no heap rewrite on either side. S14.4 inverted the lock-in — `assertFastDefaultGapReadsNullOnHostedPG` → `assertFastDefaultMaterialisesOnHostedPG` (its relid-1249 tripwire is now scoped to 1249's own rows, since a user table's fast default legitimately makes the unscoped count non-zero). - [x] **M0131-S15 — Runtime `CREATE DATABASE` must lay down the critical system indexes** (DONE 2026-08-12, design `0131-0032`). **The filed hypothesis below is REFUTED and that is the discovery:** the runtime path does NOT clone "only what goopg needs" — `CreatePerDatabaseScaffolding`/`copyBootstrapCatalogImage` already copies template0's ENTIRE on-disk image; **template0 itself was the stale one**. `bootstrapPostgresDatabase` materialises `base/4` EARLY in `Init` (copying a `base/1` the btree bulk-loaders have not written yet) and then stamps 1-page metapage-only placeholders over its per-database index OIDs, while the ~40 bootstrappers that follow target `base/1` and `base/5` explicitly and never revisit it. Measured on a fresh `goopg init`: `base/4` = 89 files with an **8192-byte** `2662`, against `base/5` = 149 files with 16384 — 59 files missing outright (the `pg_proc` heap 1255 among them) and 35 more stale. Source is `base/5` not `base/1` because it is the superset (it has `pg_filenode.map` and the shared-index placeholder files `base/4` must keep). Guards: `TestTemplate0ImageMatchesPostgresDatabase` (`internal/initdb/template0_image_test.go`) asserts whole-directory equality plus a size floor on `2662` so a future change making both dirs equally EMPTY cannot pass, proven fail-when-broken (59 missing / 35 differing with the call removed); **S15.4 DONE** — the E2E lock-in is inverted to `assertHostedPGReadsGoopgCreatedDatabase`, which failed first in the fail-when-fixed direction and now reads `s4other`'s row through the hosted PG, and Guard 4's log scan gained coverage because the last probe is no longer destructive. 1 ledger row (no in-place upgrade for a pre-existing `$PGDATA`; `base/1` has no `pg_filenode.map`; template0 keeps a `pg_internal.init` upstream's lacks). ORIGINAL FILING: (est ~2-3 loops; MEASURED by M0131-S4 F4). Connecting a hosted PG to a database goopg minted at runtime fails `PANIC: could not open critical system index 2662` (`pg_class_oid_index`) — `RelationCacheInitializePhase3` nails and opens a small critical set during `InitPostgres` and a failure there is a PANIC, so the whole cluster goes down with the connection attempt. **This is about the runtime CREATE DATABASE path, not the cold start:** the `postgres` database in the SAME directory serves every other S4 assertion. `initdb` writes each bootstrapped btree into `base/1` **and** `base/5` (`internal/initdb/btree_index_bootstrap.go` throughout); the runtime path clones only what goopg itself needs, and goopg reads its catalogs without those indexes, so nothing in the goopg-only world notices. Subtasks: S15.1 enumerate PG's critical set (`relcache.c` `RelationCacheInitializePhase3` / `criticalRelcachesBuilt`, plus the shared set in Phase 2) and check each against what CREATE DATABASE copies; S15.2 decide the mechanism — copy `base/1`'s bootstrapped index files as the template (which is what upstream's `CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE` effectively does) versus re-running the bootstrappers per database; S15.3 the PANIC is on 2662 but the set is larger, so fix the set not the one index; S15.4 INVERT `assertGoopgCreatedDatabaseStillUnopenableByPG` to a direct equality.

Theme F — Crash-state cluster-directory interchange (added 2026-08-11, user directive; removes Themes A/B's clean-shutdown precondition):

**Why:** S3 and S4 both assert `DB_SHUTDOWNED` before handing the directory over, per `0130-0002` §"WAL replay constraint". Two engines are not interchangeable on a directory if the interchange only works when the previous engine exited politely. **Theme F's filing investigation found that each direction already LOSES COMMITTED DATA today** — S11 and S12 are live bug fixes, not features, and land before everything else in the theme.
**Bounds established at filing (do NOT re-plan these):** WAL segment zeroing is a non-issue — goopg zero-fills recycled segments (`internal/wal/writer.go:2369-2379`) where upstream's `InstallXLogFileSegment` does not, so goopg is strictly safer; `CheckRequiredParameterValues` is a no-op in crash recovery (every branch gated on `ArchiveRecoveryRequested`, `xlog.c:5429`/`:5442`); and empty `pg_twophase`/`pg_commit_ts`/`pg_multixact` are all fine forward (`PrescanPreparedTransactions` over an empty dir returns `nextXid`, which is what `StartupSUBTRANS` wants; `StartupCommitTs` is gated on `track_commit_timestamp=false`; `TrimMultiXact` succeeds because initdb's zeroed `pg_multixact/offsets/0000` placeholder is load-bearing). Unlogged relations having no `_init` fork is a "too durable" divergence, not corruption — ledger it, do not absorb it here.
**Theme design:** `docs/design/0131-0012-crash-state-cluster-dir-interchange.md`. Theme F is independent of Themes C/D and may proceed in parallel.

Without it, goopg starting on a PG cluster that crashed after allocating an OID block re-issues OIDs PG already gave to catalog rows. Two deviations recorded in a ledger row: goopg takes the MAX of pg_control and the WAL records where upstream *sets* exactly (its allocator is monotone with no wraparound path), and the scan starts at record zero rather than `ExportedReplayStart`. 4 new guards (`TestReplayRecognisesPGOnlyNoOpOpcodes`, `TestReplayRefusesTwoPhaseCommitOpcodes`, `TestReplayHeap2UsesHeapOpMask`, `TestReplayNextOIDFromWAL{,NoRecords}`), ALL proven fail-when-broken by scripted reverts; one pre-existing test corrected — `TestApplyRecordRejectsUnknownDecodedXLogStandbyRecord` used `XLOG_INVALIDATIONS` 0x20 as its stand-in for an *unknown* standby opcode, a value S21a-1 makes known, so it now names 0x30 which PG really leaves undefined. S28 correctly stays a self-arming skip (its refusal moves to the first page-mutating opcode). **S21a-2 PART 1 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_HEAP2_MULTI_INSERT` + the replay gap.** `replayDecodedXLogHeapMultiInsert` mirrors `heap_xlog_multi_insert` (heapam_xlog.c:600-731): **both** main-data layouts — the `offsets[]` array is present ONLY when `XLOG_HEAP_INIT_PAGE` is clear, and with the bit set tuples land at `FirstOffsetNumber+i` (reading the wrong layout is silent corruption, not a decode error, so each has its own guard) — the SHORTALIGNed `xl_multi_insert_tuple` walk with upstream's exact-consumption check ("total tuple length mismatch": a short walk means a dropped tuple while replay reports success), the `PD_ALL_VISIBLE` page-header mirroring of `XLH_INSERT_ALL_VISIBLE_CLEARED`/`ALL_FROZEN_SET`, and FPI restore. The per-tuple rebuild is byte-identical to the single-tuple insert path, so the two now share `buildTupleFromXLogHeapHeader` (`xl_multi_insert_tuple[2:7]` IS `xl_heap_header`). **The replay gap closed on BOTH heap paths at once** via the new shared `redoHeapPageForBlock`: a block past the fork's flushed length is not an error — the primary's extension is not WAL-logged, so a crash tail routinely references one — and upstream zero-extends up to it (`XLogReadBufferExtended`, xlogutils.c:479-539) where goopg refused the whole start with "xlog heap-insert replay gap". One deviation, ledger row: goopg refuses (never mis-applies) a multi-insert onto an ALREADY-ALLOCATED line pointer, because `PageInsertItemRawAt` would shift the array where upstream's `PageAddItem(overwrite=true)` refills in place; the missing primitive is in `internal/storage`, not the WAL layer. 6 new guards / 9 subtests in `internal/wal/heap_multi_insert_pg_test.go`, ALL proven fail-when-broken by 5 scripted reverts. **S21a-2 PART 2 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_HEAP_LOCK` + `XLOG_HEAP_CONFIRM`.** The two remaining RM_HEAP page mutations, one slice because both stamp a single tuple header on an already-existing page. `replayDecodedXLogHeapLock` mirrors `heap_xlog_lock`: `xl_heap_lock` decode, `xlogHeapLockInfomaskBits` (goopg's port of `fix_infomask_from_infobits`), and the new `storage.PageApplyHeapLockRedo` — the **redo sibling** of the runtime `PageSetHeapTupleLockOnly`, separate on purpose because redo must reproduce whatever PG decided (a multixact xmax, an updater's key-share lock) rather than the single lock-only xid goopg itself takes. It clears `HEAP_XMAX_BITS|HEAP_MOVED` + `HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED`, ORs the record's bits, and **when the result is locked-only clears `HEAP_HOT_UPDATED` and re-points `t_ctid` at the tuple itself** (a locker must not leave a forward chain link behind — taking that branch when the xmax is an updater's, or skipping it when it is not, is silent corruption, so each shape has its own guard), then stamps xmax and `cmax = FirstCommandId`. `isHeapXmaxLockedOnlyPG` is upstream's `HEAP_XMAX_IS_LOCKED_ONLY` in FULL, incl. the pre-9.3 bare-EXCL_LOCK clause the exported `IsHeapTupleLockOnly` omits (that one is the goopg-tuple shortcut; redo classifies tuples PG wrote). `HeapMovedOff/In` and `HeapXmaxBits` are named in `internal/storage` for the first time — goopg never sets HEAP_MOVED, but redo must still clear it or a pg_upgrade'd tuple's `t_field3` survives as a cmax. `replayDecodedXLogHeapConfirm` overwrites the speculative token a spec-insert leaves in `t_ctid` with the self-pointer. **New `redoExistingHeapPageForBlock` is the RBM_NORMAL sibling of part 1's `redoHeapPageForBlock`**: a block past the fork length or an all-zero page is SKIPPED (BLK_NOTFOUND, `xlogutils.c:500-540`), never zero-extended — the asymmetry is upstream's, since a pure tuple stamp can only find its page missing if the relation is dropped later in the same stream. 8 guards / 9 subtests in `internal/wal/heap_lock_confirm_pg_test.go`, ALL proven fail-when-broken by 6 scripted reverts. Also fixed: part 1's `TestReplayPGHeapMultiInsertRefusesLinePointerReuse` seeded from a **map literal**, so Go's randomised iteration order failed it on ~half of all runs ("slot 2 out of range") — ordered slice now. 2 ledger rows (no invalid-page table; `XLH_LOCK_ALL_FROZEN_CLEARED` not acted on — both resume in the VISIBLE slice). **S21a-2 PART 3 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_HEAP2_VISIBLE` + the VM fork.** Every VACUUM emits one per page it marks all-visible (and an INSERT that freezes a page it filled emits one too), with 0% reuse from goopg's native `RecordKindHeapVisible` no-op, and it is the FIRST goopg redo to write a fork other than `main`. `replayDecodedXLogHeap2Visible` mirrors `heap_xlog_visible` (heapam_xlog.c): block 1's heap page gets `PD_ALL_VISIBLE`, block 0's visibility-map page gets the record's bits, and **the halves are independent** — upstream's "if the heap file has dropped or truncated later in recovery, we don't need to update the page, but we'd better still update the visibility map", so the heap-side `redoExistingHeapPageForBlock` skip must not skip the map. New `redoVMPageForBlock` is the `RBM_ZERO_ON_ERROR` member of the `redo*PageForBlock` family (a vm fork shorter than the referenced block is initialised on the spot, not a replay gap — vm extensions are no more WAL-logged than heap ones). **The "thread a VM handle into replay" premise from part 2 turned out to be wrong and better:** `ApplyRecord` needs no `*storage.VisibilityMap`, because crash recovery replays at `initdb/open.go:380` while `VMLoadForks` populates `Runtime.VM` at `:2472` — a redo that mutated the in-memory map would be *overwritten* by that load, whereas the on-disk `_vm` fork is picked up by it; the fork layout was already PG's, so only the addressing arithmetic was new (`internal/storage/vm_redo.go` ports `HEAPBLK_TO_MAPBLOCK`/`MAPBYTE`/`OFFSET` + the `visibilitymap_set` OR with upstream's `flags != status` short-circuit and the `visibilitymap_clear` AND-NOT that refuses to clear ALL_VISIBLE alone). `VISIBILITYMAP_XLOG_CATALOG_REL` is wire-only and masked off; a flags byte outside `VISIBILITYMAP_XLOG_VALID_BITS` refuses where upstream merely asserts. **Part 2's `XLH_LOCK_ALL_FROZEN_CLEARED` deferral is discharged**, in upstream's position: `heap_xlog_lock` clears the block's ALL_FROZEN bit BEFORE and independently of the heap page redo ("the visibility map may need to be fixed even if the heap page is already up-to-date"), so a pd_lsn-skipped lock record still fixes the map — its own guard, since the alternative leaves an index-only scan trusting a frozen bit for a page that now carries a live locker. 6 guards / 8 subtests in `internal/wal/heap_visible_pg_test.go` + 4 in `internal/storage/vm_redo_test.go`, ALL proven fail-when-broken by 6 scripted reverts. 4 deferrals in one ledger row: hot-standby snapshot-conflict resolution, upstream's FSM free-space update, `VMSaveForks` dropping ALL_FROZEN (the in-memory VM is `[]bool`), and the deliberate no-extend on a clear. **S21a-2 PART 4 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_HEAP2_LOCK_UPDATED`.** `heap_xlog_lock_updated`'s near-sibling relationship to part 2's `heap_xlog_lock` is exact at the wire level — `xl_heap_lock_updated` is byte-identical to `xl_heap_lock`, so `replayDecodedXLogHeap2LockUpdated` reuses `decodeXLogHeapLockMainData`, `xlogHeapLockInfomaskBits`, `redoExistingHeapPageForBlock`, and the `XLH_LOCK_ALL_FROZEN_CLEARED` → `redoClearVMBitsForHeapBlock` call verbatim — but the tuple mutation itself is deliberately smaller: new `storage.PageApplyHeapLockUpdatedRedo` clears `HEAP_XMAX_BITS|HEAP_MOVED`, ORs in the record's bits, and stamps xmax, but (unlike `PageApplyHeapLockRedo`) never touches `t_ctid`/`HEAP_HOT_UPDATED` and never stamps `cmax` — upstream's redo for this opcode has no locked-only branch and no cmax write at all, because re-locking an *older* version of an update chain (which is what this opcode means: the original lock target was concurrently updated, so the locker re-locks the newest visible version instead) can never legitimately claim to be the chain head or the locker's own command target. 7 guards in `internal/wal/heap_lock_updated_pg_test.go`, ALL proven fail-when-broken by 3 scripted reverts (ctid/HOT-bit stamp, cmax stamp, dispatch wiring). **S21a-2 PART 5 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `CLOG_ZEROPAGE`.** RM_CLOG's `WriteZeroPageXlogRec` opcode (0x00), fired once per 32768 XIDs right before the first commit/abort into a fresh CLOG page. Unlike `CLOG_TRUNCATE` it needs no `*mvcc.CLog`/catalog handle — it is pure page-zeroing at a fixed segment offset — so `replayDecodedXLogClogZeroPage` runs directly in the physical pass (`initdb/open.go:380`, well before `mvcc.OpenCLog` at `:1006`) rather than deferring to `replayCLogFromWAL`'s initdb second pass. It writes a zero-filled BLCKSZ page into the `pg_xact/` segment named `"%04X"` of `pageno/32` at offset `(pageno%32)*BLCKSZ`, creating the segment if absent — a deliberate small duplication of `clogBufferPool.segPathForPage`'s arithmetic (`wal` cannot import `internal/mvcc`; the reverse import already exists for the async-commit WAL-flush hook). **Why an arm is needed at all, given goopg's own CLOG fault-in already zero-fills a missing/short segment (`clogBufferPool.readPageFromDisk`) and so silently dropping this record was accidentally harmless for goopg's own reads:** upstream `SimpleLruReadPage` hard-errors on a missing segment rather than zero-filling, so a real PG standby cold-starting on a goopg-written cluster, or any tool reading `pg_xact/` directly (`pg_resetwal`, `amcheck`), needs the segment to physically exist for every XID range ever assigned — a crashed real PG's WAL tail that allocated a fresh CLOG page left that segment absent. 2 guards in `internal/wal/clog_zeropage_pg_test.go` (fresh low-segment page; a high-segment pageno names its segment file correctly and does not disturb segment 0), proven fail-when-broken by a scripted revert of the dispatch case. **S21a-2 PART 6 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_SMGR_TRUNCATE`.** RM_SMGR's 0x20 opcode — the physical half of every TABLE/INDEX TRUNCATE and every VACUUM tail truncation (`XLOG_HEAP_TRUNCATE` above is the logical-decoding-only no-op; the real shrink arrives here, `heapam_xlog.c:1201-1208`). goopg's own native `RecordKindSmgrTruncate`/`replaySmgrTruncate` always drops a relfile to zero blocks and its decoder carries no `blkno`/fork bitmask — a real PG's VACUUM tail truncation is a genuinely partial shrink of the main fork plus an independent zeroing of the vm/fsm forks, which those primitives cannot express. Two new pieces: `storage.relFile.truncateTo`/`Manager.TruncateRelationTo(rel, n)` (idempotent — no-op if the file is already `<= n` blocks, mirroring `TruncateRelation`'s zero-block idempotency) alongside the decoder `decodeXLogSmgrTruncate` (`BlockNumber blkno` + `RelFileLocator` + `int flags`, 20 bytes, `storage_xlog.h:46-51`, reusing `decodeXLogSmgrCreate`'s default/global-tablespace-OID remap to goopg's TblOid=0 convention). `applySmgrTruncate` mirrors `smgr_redo`'s exact order: forcibly `applySmgrCreate`s the main fork first (a later-dropped relation still gets its truncate replayed, matching upstream's "prefer to recreate the rel … until the drop is seen"), then truncates main to `blkno` under `SMGR_TRUNCATE_HEAP`, vm to 0 under `_VM`, fsm to 0 under `_FSM`, each flag independent. Deliberate deviation needing no ledger row: upstream's pre-truncate `XLogFlush(lsn)` is a live-server torn-truncate durability guard with no counterpart in goopg's single-threaded startup replay pass. 4 guards in `internal/wal/smgr_truncate_pg_test.go` (partial main-fork truncate to a non-zero blkno, idempotent on replay; VM-only flag leaves main/fsm untouched; a truncate naming a relation with no on-disk main fork recreates it then truncates per the flags; tablespace-OID remap round-trip), ALL proven fail-when-broken by a scripted revert of the dispatch case. **S21a-2 PART 7 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `XLOG_HEAP2_REWRITE`'s loud refusal, CLOSING S21a-2.** RM_HEAP2's 0x00, the only S21a-2 opcode whose landing is a refusal rather than a redo. PG emits it while a `VACUUM FULL`/`CLUSTER` rewrites a table whose pre-rewrite row versions a logical replication slot may still have to decode (`rewriteheap.c:894`, reachable only via `logical_rewrite_log_mapping` — `wal_level=logical` plus a slot that can reach the relation), and its redo touches no relation page at all: it truncates a `pg_logical/mappings/` file to the record's `offset`, rewrites the old-ctid→new-ctid mapping tail and fsyncs (`heap_xlog_logical_rewrite`, `rewriteheap.c:1073-1160`). goopg has no `pg_logical/mappings` consumer, so neither alternative is honest — implementing the redo maintains a file nothing reads (a half implementation whose only effect is hiding the gap), and recognising it as a no-op the way `HEAP2_NEW_CID` is would leave a slot on the resulting cluster decoding the rewritten table against mappings that stop mid-rewrite with nothing reporting an error. The arm returns `ErrUnsupportedRecord` + a message naming the feature (same shape as the 2PC refusal); the class matters because it is what stops the reader treating a durable record as a torn tail (`format.go`, S16.2) — before this arm the record fell to RM_HEAP2's `default:`, whose bare error carries no class. 3 guards in `internal/wal/heap2_rewrite_pg_test.go` (dispatch-level refusal + wording; a real-shaped 40-byte `xl_heap_rewrite_mapping` record driven through encode→decode→`ApplyRecord` hits the refusal rather than an earlier decode error; `HEAP2_NEW_CID` still returns `(false, nil)` so the new arm has not swallowed its neighbour), proven fail-when-broken by a scripted revert of the dispatch case. One ledger row for the unimplemented mapping-file redo. **S21b PART 1 LANDED 2026-08-12 — `INSERT_UPPER` 0x10 + `INSERT_META` 0x20 + `META_CLEANUP` 0xE0.** The three btree opcodes whose whole redo is a downlink insert and/or a metapage rewrite — no new page primitive, which is what makes them one coherent slice. `replayDecodedXLogBtreeInsert` grew upstream's own arguments (the function is literally `btree_xlog_insert(isleaf, ismeta, posting)`, nbtxlog.c:160-247, instantiated four ways; goopg already had `(true,false,false)`) plus two limbs in upstream's order: block 1 when `!isleaf` — an insert into an INTERNAL page IS the completion of the child's split, so redo clears the child's `BTP_INCOMPLETE_SPLIT`; goopg REFUSES a record missing block 1 rather than skipping the limb, because `_bt_insertonpg` registers `cbuf` unconditionally on that path (nbtinsert.c:1342-1343) and upstream PANICs on an unregistered id, so a skip would leave a permanently half-split child while replay reported success; and block 2 when `ismeta` — the WILL_INIT metapage rebuilt from the carried `xl_btree_metadata`. **The block-0 image branch must NOT return early** (the shape the pre-S21b one-limb insert replay had): upstream's `XLogReadBufferForRedo` reports BLK_RESTORED for block 0 only and still reaches `if (ismeta) _bt_restore_meta(record, 2)`, so returning after the image restore leaves the metapage naming a stale root with replay reporting success — its own guard. `_bt_restore_meta` became the shared `replayDecodedXLogBtreeRestoreMeta(…, blockID, what)` because three call sites need it on TWO different block ids (2 for INSERT_META and NEWROOT, **0** for META_CLEANUP) — hard-coding the id, the obvious refactor, would silently rebuild the wrong page; NEWROOT's metapage limb folded onto it unchanged (its error strings were already identical). 5 guards in `internal/wal/btree_insert_upper_pg_test.go`, ALL proven fail-when-broken by 4 scripted reverts (dropped child limb → 2 FAIL; early return on a block-0 image → 1 FAIL; META_CLEANUP reading block 2 → 1 FAIL; all three dispatch arms removed → 5 FAIL). **Correction to the S21a-2 closing note:** `REUSE_PAGE` 0xD0 was NOT recognised in S21a-1 (its six no-ops are all RM_HEAP/HEAP2/XACT/STANDBY); it still hits the `default:` refusal and is part 3's work. **S21b part 2a landed 2026-08-12:** `XLOG_BTREE_INSERT_POST` (0x50) — the leaf insert whose heap TID fell INSIDE an existing posting list, so the primary SPLIT that posting (`_bt_insertonpg`'s `postingoff > 0` path). goopg never emits it (its duplicate-key inserts APPEND via `appendTIDToPosting`) but deduplication is ON BY DEFAULT in every real PG index whose opclass allows it, so it is ordinary crash-tail traffic. The non-obvious part: **the record does not carry the item that ends up on the page** — block 0's data run is `{uint16 postingoff, orignewitem}`, and redo must re-run `_bt_swap_posting`, which grows NOTHING: the posting keeps its exact byte length and TID count, its rightmost/max TID falls off the end, `orignewitem`'s TID fills the gap at `postingoff`, and the EVICTED max TID becomes the final new item's `t_tid`. Inserting `orignewitem` verbatim leaves both items holding the wrong TID — an index that scans wrong rather than one that fails to start. goopg's first posting-list WRITERS landed in `internal/access/btree/posting.go`: `SwapPosting` (`_bt_swap_posting`) and the exported `PGBTPostingRaw` (`_bt_form_posting`), the latter now the ONE tuple-format posting encoder (`marshalPosting` delegates; byte-identical, no on-disk bytes move). `btree.ApplyInsertPostingRecordAt` is the page-level redo; `replayDecodedXLogBtreeInsert` grew the third upstream argument `posting` and is now instantiated all four ways. Refusals BEFORE the page is touched for `postingoff` outside `(0, nhtids)`, a non-posting left neighbour, and `offnum < 2` (whose unchecked `offnum-1` underflows to 65535). 5 guards in `internal/wal/btree_insert_post_pg_test.go` (incl. the FPI shape: restore the image, do NOT re-run the split on top), proven fail-when-broken by 2 scripted reverts. **S21b part 2b landed 2026-08-12** — `DEDUP` 0x60, the leaf deduplication pass and the most common PG-only btree opcode in a crash tail (dedup is the default for every opclass that allows it; it is the record S16.3 named when it made the FPI-only `default:` a refusal). The record carries NO tuples — `xl_btree_dedup{nintervals}` plus a block-0 array of `BTDedupInterval{baseoff, nitems}` — so redo REBUILDS the page from its own pre-image: `btree.ReplayDedupPage` collapses each interval's run into one posting via `PGBTPostingRaw` (`_bt_form_posting`) and copies the rest verbatim, where upstream re-runs its dedup state machine under the same bounds. Two traps, both yielding the right item COUNT when got wrong: `nitems` counts ITEMS not heap TIDs (a run's base may already be a posting, contributing several TIDs — upstream's `basetupsize = BTreeTupleGetPostingOffset(base)`), and the high key must NOT be re-added because `resetPageItems` re-installs it for every rewrite path in the package. `BTP_HAS_GARBAGE` cleared as upstream does; FPI branch restores and stops. Refusals before the page is touched for a short interval array vs the record's own `nintervals`, an unmatched `baseoff`, a one-item run, an overrunning run, a pivot inside a run. 6 guards in `internal/wal/btree_dedup_pg_test.go`, proven fail-when-broken by 2 scripted reverts. **S21b part 3 landed 2026-08-12 and CLOSES S21b** — `DELETE` 0x70, the LP_DEAD simple-deletion pass (`_bt_delitems_delete`, nbtpage.c:1369: an index scan marks the entry it finds dead, the next insert short of room deletes the marked ones), plus `REUSE_PAGE` 0xD0 as a NAMED no-op — upstream's `btree_xlog_reuse_page` (nbtxlog.c:1006-1015) is one `if (InHotStandby)` conflict resolve and registers no blocks at all, which is exactly why it could not stay on the S16.3 `default:` arm that demands an applicable image on EVERY block. The substance is `btree_xlog_updates` (:556-597): a posting list's TIDs die ONE AT A TIME, so the tuple is rewritten without them rather than deleted, and `updatePostingRaw` reproduces `_bt_update_posting`'s two outcomes — re-form a posting sized exactly as `_bt_form_posting` would, or, for a SINGLE survivor, collapse back to a plain non-pivot tuple (alt-TID bit off, survivor's heap TID in `t_tid`, size back to `keysize`); a one-entry posting is a tuple no PG writes and every reader keys off BT_IS_POSTING. Updates apply BEFORE the deletions because both offset arrays are in the PRE-deletion coordinate space — deleting first shifts every later offset down and rewrites the wrong tuples. **Sibling path fixed in the same slice:** `xl_btree_vacuum` carries the same payload and does the same page work, and goopg REFUSED its `nupdated > 0` form outright, so a real PG's VACUUM records were failing the start on the same missing primitive; both opcodes now share `decodeXLogBtreeDeletePayload` + `btree.ReplayDeletePage`. RM_BTREE's opcode space is now COMPLETE (every nbtxlog.h value has a named arm), so the S16.3 fallback guard's probe moved from 0xD0 to the undefined 0xF0. 7 guards in `internal/wal/btree_delete_pg_test.go`, proven fail-when-broken by 3 scripted reverts (deletions before updates → 2 FAIL; no single-survivor collapse → 1 FAIL; `xl_btree_update` decode dropped → 4 FAIL). Ledger row for what goopg still does not EMIT (no LP_DEAD deletion pass, no dedup pass, no hot-standby conflict resolution). Gates: `internal/wal` PASS + `-race` PASS, `internal/storage` PASS, UNITS, pgbench smoke via the commit hook. Design: `docs/design/0131-0015-pg-wal-opcode-coverage.md` (**note: the file is `0131-0015`, not `0131-0014` — 0014 is the pg_control doc**) §"S21a-1 / S21a-2 — implementation notes". **S21 CLOSED 2026-08-12 — the whole opcode space asserted at once, and one defect found by asserting it.** Fourteen S21a/S21b slices each landed an opcode with its own behavioural guard; none could answer the milestone's own question, which is whether any opcode PG 18 defines inside a handled rmgr STILL falls to that rmgr's `default:`. `TestReplayOpcodeSpaceCoverageForHandledRmgrs` (`internal/wal/opcode_space_coverage_pg_test.go`) enumerates upstream's space for all **16 rmgrs with a dispatch arm** — XLOG/XACT/SMGR/CLOG/DBASE/TBLSPC/RELMAP/STANDBY/HEAP2/HEAP/BTREE/SEQ/COMMIT_TS/REPLORIGIN/GENERIC/LOGICALMSG, **74 opcode probes** cross-checked against every `#define XLOG_*` in `postgres/src/include` — and the answer is **zero holes**: S21a and S21b are complete as specified, now machine-checked rather than read off this file. Probes are header-only because this is a DISPATCH test, so any error but the default arm's own is a pass; that forces an EXACT message match rather than `errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupportedRecord)`, since the deliberate refusals (2PC, `HEAP2_REWRITE`, commit_ts-tracked) carry the same sentinel on purpose. **The defect is in the controls:** each rmgr also probes a value PG leaves undefined, which must land on `default:` — and 13 of the 14 failed, 12 for one cause: **only RM_XLOG's `default:` carried `ErrUnsupportedRecord`**, the other thirteen returned a bare error. That contradicts `format.go:45-56` (an unsupported record is durable, categorically unlike a torn tail, and a caller must be able to tell them apart) and is the exact hazard S21a-2 part 7 named. It survived fourteen slices because nothing observable changed — both `ApplyRecord` callers refuse the start on ANY error — which is the argument for pinning it now rather than after the first caller that discriminates. All 16 default arms now route through the new `unsupportedDecodedXLogOpcode` (`internal/wal/recovery.go`). RM_BTREE's control expects different wording on purpose: its `default:` is S16.3's FPI fallback, not a bare refusal. Out of scope and stated, not assumed: RM_HASH/GIN/GIST/SPGIST/BRIN are refused WHOLESALE by rmgr (S25), so enumerating their opcodes would assert the opposite of what S25 decided; RM_MULTIXACT has no arm at all and is S24's open work. No new ledger row — nothing PG-behavioural was deferred by this slice. Both halves proven fail-when-broken by scripted reverts (drop the `XLOG_HEAP_INPLACE` arm → 1 FAIL naming it; drop the class → 13 control FAILs). Gates: `internal/wal` PASS + `-race` PASS, `internal/initdb` PASS, UNITS, pgbench smoke via the commit hook. Design `0131-0015` §"S21 closure".
- [x] **M0131-S22 — CLOG replay opcode dispatch + commit-record `subxacts[]` parsing** (**DONE 2026-08-12**) (est ~1 loop). A separate second WAL pass with its own bug: `internal/initdb/xact_recovery.go:87-92` treats ANY `RmgrXact` record with a non-zero XID as commit-or-abort (`isCommit := (Info & XlogXactOpMask) == XlogXactCommit`), so a PG `XLOG_XACT_ASSIGNMENT` (0x50), `PREPARE` (0x10) or `COMMIT_PREPARED` (0x30) is **stamped ABORTED**. Separately goopg never parses the commit record's `subxacts[]` array, so **subtransactions of a committed top-level xact are never stamped committed** and their rows stay invisible after a reverse crash start. Dispatch on the opcode and parse the array. Gate: a unit test over a captured PG commit record carrying subxacts, plus an E2E whose PG workload uses a SAVEPOINT before the kill. - [x] **M0131-S26 — `pd_lsn` completeness audit on logged change paths** (est ~2 loops). PG's crash recovery replays over live data files whose pages may already be AHEAD of the record and skips them via `if (lsn <= PageGetLSN(page)) return BLK_DONE;`. If any goopg **logged** mutation dirties a page without stamping `pd_lsn` to the emitting record's end LSN, PG double-applies — a duplicated row or a btree unique violation, not a crash. Streaming from a base backup barely exercises this; crash recovery does so constantly. Audit every `Pool.MarkDirty*` variant against its `SetLSN` (`internal/storage/bufpool.go:2091-2340`, 9 `SetLSN` sites) and every `logXxx` hook (`internal/initdb/open.go:430-745`); add a debug assertion. Document that `MarkDirtyHint` deliberately does NOT bump `pd_lsn` (`internal/storage/bufpool.go:2053-2057`) and that this exception is PG-faithful because hint bits are recomputable — the question is whether any *logged* path shares it. Plain `MarkDirty` advances `pd_lsn` only as a side effect of the first-touch FPI, so on an already-imaged (hot catalog) page the stamp was left behind its own record — breaking WAL-before-data (`flushSlots` flushes only to `max(pd_lsn)`) and making a replaying PG re-apply (`lsn <= PageGetLSN(page)`). Fixed with a new `Pool.MarkDirtyCoveredByRecordLocked`, whose contract is the non-obvious part: image first, RAISE `pd_lsn` (never lower — `maybeEmitFPI` may have just stamped a larger one), and do NOT advance `nativeImageLSN`, because no image of that page exists at the record's LSN and moving the watermark would suppress its next first-touch FPI. Guards `internal/storage/pdlsn_secondary_page_test.go` + `internal/executor/pdlsn_cross_page_update_test.go` (fail-when-broken proven: reverting the call site reports `old page pd_lsn = 1001, still behind the covering xl_heap_update at 1002`). **DONE 2026-08-12 (loop #21):** the remaining two pieces landed. The class-B sites moved to a new `Pool.MarkDirtyUnlogged(s, reason)` (2× multixact lock stamp, `pg_database` datconnlimit + datfrozenxid) so the report is only the sites that still need classifying. Guards `internal/storage/pdlsn_assert_test.go` (fires for plain MarkDirty under a wired pool; silent for the stamping/unlogged/hint variants; silent when WAL is unwired; off by default). Empirically: pgbench -i -s2 + 20s/4 clients (12 783 txns) + VACUUM + CREATE INDEX + a 20 000-row UPDATE on a capped server → **zero reports**, and arming was PROVEN rather than assumed (a temporary probe in `MarkDirtyLogicalChange` produced `PDLSN-UNSTAMPED … site=…markHeapInsertDirty (operators_storage.go:9387)`; both probes reverted). (b) The `logXxx`-hook audit: five hooks register >1 block (btree split/newroot/unlink/markhalfdead, heap update) and on the pd_lsn axis they are CLEAN — every named block is stamped with the record's LSN by its caller. It did surface an adjacent-axis gap, filed as S26b below. Ledger 2026-08-12 ×3.

Scaling: clients 1/2/4/8 -> lost 6589/1/3599/10520 of the committed updates; the single-client row is the important one. **Rides along:** after the stall the index read `WHERE id=1` returns NOTHING while the seq read `WHERE id+0=1` returns the stale row — the S31 signature (`0131-0019`) reappearing, so `hotstall.sh` reports both reads and the two must never be conflated. **Ruled out by inspection, do not re-test:** `tryApplyHOTUpdate` (`internal/executor/operators_storage.go:3555`) DOES re-read the old tuple under the exclusive content lock and call `isConcurrentlyUpdated` before stamping; `isConcurrentlyUpdated` (`:3180`) returns true for a *committed* foreign xmax as well as an in-progress one (it excludes only aborted); and the `!used` fallback runs a full EPQ retry loop with RC chain-following (`:4328`). Independently of the cause, the statement reports `UPDATE 1` while writing nothing, so the row count is coming from the planned row set rather than from rows actually written; upstream `heap_update` (`postgres/src/backend/access/heap/heapam.c`) has no 'success, nothing written' outcome at all. One HOT update = one chain link, so version 65 sat at depth 65 and the walk gave up before reaching it: the index scan driving the UPDATE found no live tuple, wrote NOTHING, and still reported `UPDATE 1` (the count comes from the planned row set); `WHERE id=1` returned nothing while the seq read returned version 64 with an unstamped xmax — so the "S31 index-unreachable signature" here was a CONSEQUENCE of the same truncation, not a second defect; and `pruneChainTip` gave up at the same depth, never reclaiming the dead versions, which is what made the boundary look like page capacity. When the old-slot stamp fails, `tryApplyHOTUpdate` calls `storage.PageRemoveHeapTuple(s.Page(), newSlot)` (`internal/executor/operators_storage.go:3746`) and emits nothing — while the `PagePruneOpt` that usually CAUSED the failure was logged via `markHeapPruneOptDirty`. `PageRemoveHeapTuple` does not only blank the line pointer: when the removed slot is the last one it SHRINKS `pd_lower` (`internal/storage/heap.go:697-699`), reducing the page's line-pointer count. The slot is already dirty from the logged prune, so the mutation reaches disk and replay rebuilds a LARGER page than the runtime had — a runtime/WAL page divergence of exactly the S30.3 family (one line pointer per occurrence, so it does not by itself explain 185 -> 1). Upstream has no unlogged heap-page mutation of this kind: `PageRepairFragmentation` truncates trailing unused line pointers only inside a WAL-logged vacuum/prune under a cleanup lock (`postgres/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c`). Fix candidates: reuse `markHeapPruneOptDirty` with a one-slot `Unused` result (check that its replay arm reproduces the `pd_lower` shrink), or stop shrinking `pd_lower` and let the next logged prune reclaim the slot. Gate: a unit test asserting replay of the emitted stream reproduces the runtime page byte-for-byte. **RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (loop #135).** Neither filed candidate was taken: both miss that the ADD is unlogged too, so the add/remove pair needs no WAL record — it needs to be a no-op on the page, and it was not. `PageAddHeapTuple` moves `pd_lower` (+4) AND `pd_upper` (-MAXALIGN(len)); `PageRemoveHeapTuple` restored only `pd_lower`, leaking one tuple's free space per occurrence out of a page the WAL says still has it. `PageRemoveHeapTuple` (`internal/storage/heap.go`) now also raises `pd_upper` back over the item body when the removed slot is the last line pointer and its body sits exactly at `pd_upper` — the state an append leaves, making the call an exact inverse; interior removals are unchanged. The vacated bytes fall back inside `[pd_lower, pd_upper)`, PG's FPI hole, so they are outside the page image either way. Guards `TestPageRemoveHeapTupleUndoesAppend` (fails pre-fix: `pd_upper=8056 want=8096`) / `TestPageRemoveHeapTupleInteriorSlotKeepsUpper` in `internal/storage/heap_test.go`. One same-family divergence in this arm stays open (ledger 2026-08-11): a successful old-slot multixact stamp followed by a failing `PageSetHeapTupleCmax` leaves the old tuple's xmax mutated with no WAL. Design `docs/design/0131-0021` §Update 2026-08-11 (loop #135).

This is both why the volume reaches the segment boundary and why a truncated replay costs so many rows. **DECIDED 2026-08-12 (loop #152)** — `docs/design/0131-0031`. Verdict: **the probe is correct and the trigger works.** `analysis/crashprobe.sh` writes no `postgresql.conf` overrides, so it runs at the PG defaults (`checkpoint_timeout` 300 s, `max_wal_size` 1024 MB, `checkpoint_completion_target` 0.9) and is killed 30 s in — a real PG under the same workload also produces zero checkpoints, and ~180 MiB is below any volume threshold either engine uses. Zero checkpoints is an artifact of the probe's DURATION, exactly the aggravating factor this item suspected, not a broken checkpointer. Establishing that exposed three real `max_wal_size` deviations, all fixed here: (1) goopg used `max_wal_size` AS the trigger distance where upstream's `CalculateCheckpointSegments` (xlog.c:2170-2198) divides it by `1 + checkpoint_completion_target` and `XLogCheckpointNeeded` fires `CheckPointSegments - 1` **segments** past redo — at the shared defaults PG checkpoints every 512 MiB, goopg waited 1024 MiB; (2) the anchor was the checkpoint RECORD's end LSN rather than `RedoRecPtr`, shortening every window after the first by the flush phase plus the `XLOG_RUNNING_XACTS` record (`Run` now seeds a start-position anchor for the pre-first-checkpoint window, so a restart above `max_wal_size` no longer checkpoints on the first poll); (3) found by measurement — at `CheckPointSegments == 1` the literal `elapsed >= 0` test plus goopg's 1 s poll (upstream evaluates only at a segment switch) gave **42 checkpoints in 40 s** of pgbench, so the polled distance now floors at one segment (re-measured: 14 checkpoints over ~223 MiB, one per segment). Guards `TestCheckpointerCheckPointSegments` (pins the PG-default 33-segment/512 MiB row), rewritten `TestCheckpointerVolumeTriggerThreshold`, `TestCheckpointerVolumeTriggerDisabled`. DEFERRED (ledger row): the volume condition is still polled rather than signalled from the writer's segment switch, and neither `max_wal_size` nor `checkpoint_completion_target` recomputes the distance on a GUC reload.

## M0132 — Explicit transactions across the extended query protocol (filed 2026-08-12, user directive)

**Priority: PROMOTED (user directive 2026-08-13) — next after M-NIGHTLY.** The `## Current Priority` banner at the top of this file names M0132 first after M-NIGHTLY's standing filing obligation; work M0132 tasks immediately after M-NIGHTLY's regression fixes, ahead of M0131 and M0130's remaining items.

Milestone: `docs/milestones/0132-extended-protocol-explicit-transactions.md`. Authoritative decomposition: `docs/design/0132-extended-protocol-explicit-transactions.md`. Core design: `docs/design/0132-0001-extended-protocol-explicit-txn-state-machine.md`. Supersedes (on landing) the `design`-status sketch `analysis/perf-optimize3-dash/08-improvement-designs/09-extended-protocol-explicit-txn.md` (2026-07-14) and discharges `.ralph/deferral_ledger.md:347`, the 2026-07-14 row deferring it because "a partial land would silently skip INITIALLY DEFERRED constraints".

**The bug, verified at HEAD `28de7c44` (2026-08-12).** goopg's extended query protocol (Parse/Bind/Execute) begins and commits its own transaction on **every** `Execute`, and treats the client's `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` as accepted-but-ignored command tags — `dispatch_extended.go:110-112` returns a bare `CommandTag` for a `*planner.Transaction` node, `:134-139` unconditionally begins a fresh READ COMMITTED transaction on an offset proc slot, `:361-365` unconditionally commits it. `connTx *connTxState` is already threaded into `executeExtendedQueryViaExecutor` (`:30`) but is read only for `NonSuperuserRole` (`:36`, `:46`, `:238`, `:250`) and statement logging (`:68`, `:71`); `connTx.Begin`/`InExplicit`/`Tx`/`End` have **zero** call sites in `dispatch_extended.go` or `extended.go`. The simple path models the block (`dispatch.go:227-229` reuses `connTx.Tx()`; `:2696-2984` is the 289-line verb arm, promotion at `:2701`).

**Why it is a correctness milestone, not a perf one.** `ROLLBACK` over the extended protocol **does not roll back** — a `BEGIN` → `UPDATE` → `UPDATE` → `ROLLBACK` sequence has already durably committed both updates when the `ROLLBACK` arrives, which returns a success tag. Atomicity across statements is lost (a failure at statement *k* leaves `1..k-1` committed); `ReadyForQuery` reports `I` where PG reports `T` (the byte comes from `connTxState.wireStatus`, `conn_tx.go:415`, installed once per connection at `server.go:1526` as `w.TxStatusFn` — an *observable protocol* divergence drivers gate on); and isolation levels above READ COMMITTED are unreachable (`:139` hardcodes RC; the comment at `:119-123` says SERIALIZABLE "cannot apply").

**The shape real drivers emit is MIXED, and worse.** pgx v5 (`conn.go:515`, "Always use simple protocol when there are no arguments") and lib/pq (`conn.go:901`) send argument-less statements — including `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` — down the **simple** path while parameterised DML goes down the extended one. So the dominant real-world shape is a block opened on the simple path with its DML executed on the extended path, producing **two live transactions on one connection**: the block held on the connection's own slot (`dispatch.go:227-229`) while each `Execute` begins and commits its own on the offset slot. The client's writes land in the auto-committing one and the `ROLLBACK` discards the empty one. Consequences: S8 (mixed) is a **primary** slice, not an edge case; acceptance bar 2b covers the driver shape; and this is a better hypothesis for S7's `mvcc: unknown transaction` aborts than "the offset scheme collides" alone.

**CORRECTION to doc 09 that reshapes S4 — there is no `execCommit` route to adopt.** Doc 09 §2/§4.1 (and the first draft of this filing) said the extended COMMIT should route through `transactionOp.execCommit`. The simple path does not use it: `dispatch.go:2803-2807` states "the simple-query dispatch bypasses transactionOp.execCommit, so the checks queued on the session during INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must be run here BEFORE TxnMgr.Commit". The deferred FK/UNIQUE/EXCLUDE passes are **inline** at `:2818-2828` (`RunDeferredFKChecks` under `FreshSnapshot`, then `RunDeferredUniqueChecks`, then `RunDeferredExclusionChecks`), the SSI pre-commit check inline after, and the arm returns at `:2980` without reaching the operator build at `:2985`. The bypass was never removed — 0119-0004 *added* the inline sequence. The extended COMMIT must inherit that sequence, which it gets **for free iff S2 is a genuine extraction**; S4 is therefore the proof obligation on S2, not independent wiring.

**LAND-TOGETHER RULE (non-negotiable): S2+S3+S4+S5 in ONE commit.** Two independent arguments, both "the half-landing opens a hole that does not exist today". (a) Without S4, a block whose COMMIT reaches `TxnMgr.Commit` by any route other than the extracted helper skips the deferred sequence and commits a block violating an `INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint — today each statement commits individually so its constraints are checked individually. (b) Without S5, an error mid-block leaves the block open and un-failed — there is **no** `connTx.Fail()` call site on the extended path (its only two are `dispatch.go:950` and `:1019`) — so post-error `Execute`s keep running in the same live transaction and `COMMIT` commits them; PG aborts everything.

**Adjacent divergences recorded but NOT closed here (ledger rows required):** (i) **COPY ignores an open block on BOTH protocols** — `copy.go:157-167`: "The COPY always runs in its own auto-commit transaction regardless of whether the client has opened an explicit BEGIN block", using the same `(ProcNum + halfSize) % ConnSlotCount` offset that S7 exists to retire (`dispatch_extended.go:136` cites copy.go as its model), so `BEGIN; COPY …; ROLLBACK` does not roll back today, simple path included; (ii) **`SET LOCAL ROLE` semantics change silently under S2** — `SnapshotLocalRoleIfNeeded` (`conn_tx.go:390-396`) returns early when `!active`, so the extended path's calls (`dispatch_extended.go:252`, `extended.go:693`, `:712`) record no restore point and `End()` never reverts; setting `active` changes that with no slice claiming it.

## M0133 — `information_schema` on disk (filed 2026-08-12, successor to the deferred M0131-S9.4)

**Priority: PROMOTED (2026-08-13) — next after M-NIGHTLY.** M0132 is complete and M0130 is closed, and M0131's only remaining `pg_catalog` work is S9.4, which this milestone IS; the `## Current Priority` banner names M0133 next after M-NIGHTLY's standing filing obligation. Work S1–S4 in order (they are serial: S4 must not begin before S1–S3 are on disk).

**Source:** M0131-S9.4, deferred 2026-08-12 with 2 ledger rows after being MEASURED rather than assumed (design `docs/design/0131-0009-system-view-corpus-widening.md` §S9.4, findings F31-F35). This section exists because a design-doc section is not a schedulable resume point: the deferral rule forbids closing with a forward reference, and "the successor decomposition is in §S9.4" is one.

**The corpus, measured against a throwaway PG 18.3 (`initdb` out of `postgres/local_install`, `pg_ctl -o "-p 5539 -k $D -h ''"`) and RE-VERIFIED against a second fresh cluster at the filing loop — all thirteen numbers reproduced exactly:** 1 `pg_namespace` row (OID **13273**), **69** `pg_class` rows (**65** views + **4** real tables), **148** `pg_type` rows (5 domains + 69 rowtypes + 74 array peers, band **13286..13621**), **696** `pg_attribute` user columns, **65** `pg_rewrite` rules totalling **1 814 056 B** of `ev_action` (max 210 908 B, `columns`), **11** `pg_proc` helpers (**13274..13285**), **2** domain CHECK constraints (`cardinal_number_domain_check`, `yes_or_no_check`) and **801 heap rows of DATA** (`sql_features` 755, `sql_sizing` 23, `sql_implementation_info` 12, `sql_parts` 11).

**Already landed by M0131-S9.4 (do not redo):** F31 — goopg registered the namespace at OID 13183 under the comment "stock PG18 initdb-assigned OID"; no run of this build produces that value. Corrected to **13273** in `internal/catalog/catalog.go` and pinned, with the measurement recipe, by `TestBootstrapNamespaceOIDsMatchPG18`.

**Three findings that shape the work:** **F32** — `pg_depend` says **zero** `information_schema` rules reference a `pg_catalog` *view*, so M0133 is independent of M0131-S9.1-S9.3 and of the 14 view-on-view edges; it is schedulable on its own. **F33** — the TOAST ceiling is already discharged (M0131-S20.2): 11 of the 65 rules exceed the ~8160 B inline budget after pglz, but the pg_catalog corpus already ships 6 toasted rules and `pg_seclabels` (35 379 B) is larger than anything here. **F34** — 10 of the 11 helpers are new-style SQL-body functions carrying `prosrc = ''` and a non-null **`prosqlbody`** `pg_node_tree`; `scripts/capture-ev-action.sh` has no `prosqlbody` mode, so this is a SECOND capture surface, not a reuse. **F35** — the 4 tables carry real rows `COPY`ed from `sql_features.txt`, a bulk-heap-load mechanism no M0131-S9 slice ever produced.

**LAND-TOGETHER CONSTRAINT (the reason S9.4 was deferred wholesale rather than dribbled):** the `information_schema` name ALREADY resolves in goopg's own front end (8 virtual relations, `registerInformationSchemaTables`, `internal/catalog/catalog.go:11613`). An on-disk namespace holding 0 of its 69 relations reports to a hosted PG a schema that exists and is empty — strictly worse than today's clean absence, and the exact half-filled-catalog anti-pattern that already bit this project (a half-filled `pg_type` broke an `IN`-list that worked at all-zero). The prerequisites are genuinely serial: the domains before any view's `pg_attribute` types resolve, the helpers before any view body does, the tables' data before `sql_features` answers. **S1-S3 may land separately; S4 must not begin before S1-S3 are all on disk, and the namespace row itself lands in S1 with its domains, atomically.**

Two helpers (`checkCommentObjectOwnerOID` for a domain's typowner, `checkCommentObjectOwner` for `catalog.Table.Owner`'s role-NAME string) raise 42501 `must be owner of {relation,type} <name>` with superuser bypass, and the table-constraint arm was refactored to OID-first resolution so the check sits between address-resolution and the `pg_description` write — PG's ordering. Scoped to the two constraint arms only; every other COMMENT ON kind stays ungated — **ledgered**. The `compatNoopCommandTag` fallback was probed and deliberately RESTORED (`dispatch.go` has zero diff): removing it reddens `TestExtendedProtocolCompatNoopCommentOnMalformed`, which pins a DIFFERENT deliberate invariant (M0097-0023, silent absorption of a truncated clause of a *supported* kind). The fallback is load-bearing for two distinct reasons — that, plus `parseCommentOnTail`'s bare `default:` for genuinely unimplemented ObjKinds (AGGREGATE/LANGUAGE/ROLE/TABLESPACE/TEXT SEARCH …, none tested) — so its stale doc comment at `dispatch.go:1800-1804` is left intact and **ledgered** rather than half-corrected.   - [x] **M0134-0005aj — `ORDER BY …::regclass` sorted by the rendered relation NAME, because the cast stringified two layers earlier** — **LANDED 2026-08-19** at the **230 / 12** baseline left by 0005ai; exits at **216 lines / 11 hunks** (hunk 12 closed, no new `@@`, no existing hunk grew). PG has **no comparison operators for `regclass` at all** (zero hits for all eleven reg* types across `postgres/src/include/catalog/{pg_operator,pg_opclass,pg_amop}.dat`); `regclass→oid` is an IMPLICIT BINARY-COERCIBLE cast (`pg_cast.dat:182-185`), so `ORDER BY` resolves through to `oid`'s btree comparator `btoidcmp` (`nbtcompare.c:441`) — an **unsigned OID** compare, with the name merely *rendered*. goopg inverted that: `internal/executor/expr.go:806-845` (the `CastExpr` arm for `regclass` with a `KindInt` source) eagerly renders the relation name via `NewStringDatum(tbl.Name)` at eval time, so `sortOp.lessRows` reached `compareDatum` (`expr.go:2651`) holding two plain strings and did `strings.Compare`. **The ordering bug is a consequence of a representation bug**, and the representation bug is wider: the eager render fires only on the `KindInt` source arm, while a string-literal source (`'pg_class'::regclass`) and real regclass-typed columns (`pg_class.reltoastrelid`, `pg_partition_tree()`) stay `KindInt` end-to-end — two disagreeing representations of one type, the sibling-divergence class. Live oracle probes proved this already yields wrong ANSWERS, not just wrong order: `oid::regclass = 1259` → goopg `f` / PG `t`, and `oid::regclass = 'pg_class'::regclass` → goopg `f` / PG `t` (two casts of the SAME relation disagree). **The root-cause fix was scoped out deliberately and is ledgered as one indivisible slice**, because the obvious "just stop stringifying" one-liner is a trap: without a matching comparison-path fix it would redden `oid::regclass IN ('a_star','c_star')` (`src/test/regress/sql/create_misc.sql:250-251`), which passes today only *coincidentally* (goopg compares name-string to name-literals; PG resolves the IN-list via `select_common_type` + `regclassin`) — a strictly worse intermediate state, not a partial fix. Doing it properly needs a static type hint on the comparison IR (`optimizer.InExpr` + the bare-`=` node) since `Datum` carries a `Kind` and no type tag, making reg*-ness unrecoverable inside `compareEq`/`promoteCrossKind`: 150-250+ lines across three packages. What landed is Sort-operator-local (`internal/executor/operators.go`, 48 lines): `isRegSortFamilyTypeName` (single membership test for the eleven reg* types, carrying the oracle citations and an explicit do-not-reuse-for-`=`/`IN`/hashing warning) and `evalSortKeyValue` (for a reg*-family `*optimizer.CastExpr` key, evaluate `.Operand` — a `KindInt` result IS the OID; otherwise evaluate the full cast, whose `KindString` arm already resolves a name to a `KindInt` OID). **Both branches yield a `KindInt` OID, so the two source shapes now sort consistently with each other** — that consistency, not merely the row order, is the point. `sortOp.lessRows` calls it for both operands, preserving the `sortErr` strict-weak-ordering discipline; ASC/DESC/NULLS untouched. `ORDER BY <ordinal>` comes free and was **verified, not assumed**: `resolveOrderBySubstitution` (`internal/optimizer/planner.go:5511`) substitutes the ordinal with the target-list AST *before* lowering to `CastExpr`, so `ORDER BY 1` — the shape the real PG corpus uses at `src/test/regress/sql/partition_prune.sql:283` — reaches the helper with the real cast node. Guards (`internal/executor/operators_regsort_test.go`, FAIL-pre/PASS-post over a fixture whose OID order and NAME order genuinely DISAGREE — one where they agree proves nothing): ASC, DESC, mixed-key tiebreak, string-source vs int-source consistency. Design §41. Gates: `go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/executor/ ./internal/optimizer/ ./internal/postmaster/` PASS, regress `constraints` 230/12 → 216/11, `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=units scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS, `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2, Q13=35 canonical — Hard-won Rule #1, executor change), pgbench smoke via the hook. Three deferrals ledgered 2026-08-19 (full Option B representation fix; unaudited hash-keying risk for GROUP BY/DISTINCT/hash-join; missing `22P02` parity on `x::regclass = '<literal>'`, a shape PG rejects via `oidin` not `regclassin`).
  - [x] **M0134-0005ak — validating a constraint validated only the table you named** — **LANDED 2026-08-19** at the **216 / 11** baseline left by 0005aj; exits at **188 lines / 9 hunks** (census hunks 10 and 11 both closed, no new `@@`, no existing hunk grew). Symptom was a stale flag: after `ALTER TABLE notnull_inhparent ALTER i SET NOT NULL`, PG reports `convalidated=t` on `notnull_inhchild`/`notnull_inhgrand` and goopg reported `f`; same shape on the partitioned tree (`notnull_tbl1_3`'s `nn3`). **goopg's own in-code comment was the misdirection** — it cited `tablecmds.c:7950-8010` and claimed PG's `ATExecSetNotNull` existing-constraint branch "returns WITHOUT recursing to children", which is true of two of the three existing-tuple sub-arms and **false of the third, the one this test exercises**: `if (!conForm->convalidated)` flips nothing itself, it delegates entirely to `ATExecValidateConstraint` (`tablecmds.c:12908`). *Validation is a different operation from marking, and it is the one that recurses.* `ATExecValidateConstraint` dispatches (`:12974-12976`) to `QueueNNConstraintValidation` (`:13220-13309`), which at the top-level call walks **`find_all_inheritors`** (`:13245-13246`) — every descendant at every depth, partitions included, NOT `find_inheritance_children`'s single level — skipping the relation itself (`:13256-13257`) and any descendant already `convalidated` (`:13277-13278`), and treating a descendant with no matching constraint as an internal `elog` invariant violation (`:13272-13274`), not a user error. goopg had **two independent gaps, not one**: the `AlterTableSetNotNull` merge branch flipped only the parent's `NotValid` and left `shouldCascade` false (the existing `cascadeNotNullToChildrenAt` call belongs to the sibling "no constraint yet" arm), and the named `ALTER TABLE … VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` NOT NULL sub-branch had the identical defect separately — fixing either alone would have left a diverging path (the sibling-path rule, paid again). Fix (`internal/executor/operators_ddl.go`, 91 lines): new `cascadeNotNullValidateToDescendants` wired at BOTH call sites, deliberately a separate helper rather than a mode flag on `cascadeNotNullToChildrenAt` (whose merge sub-branch only bumps `InhCount` and never touches `NotValid` — ADD, VALIDATE and DROP are three different operations, and DROP is already factored out for the same reason). It mirrors the DROP twins' shape (`collectInheritanceAndPartitionChildren`, edge-keyed `visited`, `maxNotNullCascadeDepth`, `syncConstraintCatalogRow` per touched child) and **self-recurses**, because goopg has no one-shot `find_all_inheritors` — only single-level `InheritanceChildren`/`PartitionChildren` (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:4489`, `:4510`). **One deliberate divergence, and it is load-bearing:** PG skips an already-`convalidated` descendant entirely; goopg flips nothing on such a child but still *recurses through* it — PG can prune because its flat `find_all_inheritors` list already contains the whole tree, so a validated intermediate node can never hide a still-unvalidated grandchild behind it, whereas goopg's level-at-a-time descent would let exactly that happen if the skip also pruned the walk. Same end state, different traversal. A descendant missing the constraint is a **skip**, not an error: goopg's catalog can legitimately reach that state and PG's `elog` there is an internal assertion, so promoting it would invent a new failure mode. Confirmed not a risk: the row-scan backing SET NOT NULL already descends the full tree (`forEachLiveRow` → `allDescendants` → `forEachLiveRowRel`), so the cascade cannot introduce a false-negative `23502`. Guards (`internal/executor/operators_ddl_notnull_validate_cascade_test.go`, FAIL-pre verified against reverted source / PASS-post): 3-level plain inheritance (`src/test/regress/sql/constraints.sql:908-917`), partitioned tree (`:920-939`), already-validated-descendant no-drift (`InhCount`/`IsLocal` untouched), and both entry points. Design §42. Gates: `go build ./...` PASS, `go test ./internal/executor/ ./internal/catalog/` PASS, named guards PASS (re-run by the coordinator before commit), regress `constraints` 216/11 → 188/9, `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=units scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS, pgbench smoke via the hook. Two deferrals ledgered 2026-08-19 (the CHECK-constraint VALIDATE cascade has the identical gap — and PG's CHECK version has NO already-convalidated skip, `tablecmds.c:13117-13210`; and PG's `ONLY`-with-children `ERRCODE_INVALID_TABLE_DEFINITION` guard at `:13260-13263`, unreproducible today because neither call site plumbs an ONLY/recurse flag this deep).

Guards: `operators_ddl_check_validate_cascade_test.go`, 10 subtests, FAIL-pre proven by stashing only the source file. Design §45. **Four rows ledgered 2026-08-19**, three of them found while writing the tests: (a) **`DELETE FROM ONLY <t>` does not honour `ONLY`** — deletes descendant rows too; newly surfaced, no prior row, a DML correctness bug and the widest blast radius of the three (it is also why the NO INHERIT scan test could not be a literal port and was split into two fixtures); (b) `catalog.AddCheckInherited` (`catalog.go:305`) stamps `NotValid=false` unconditionally, so a child inherits a `NOT VALID` parent CHECK **pre-validated** and this slice's new cascade has nothing to fix — the M0134-0005z row owns the `NotEnforced` half of the same helper's blindness, land them together; (c) PG's `ONLY`/recurse guard (`:13146-13150`) has no plumbing on `AlterTableValidateConstraint`; (d) PG skips the row re-scan of an already-`convalidated` descendant, goopg re-scans the whole tree in one pass (observable via `alter_table.sql:408-411`'s `boo()` NOTICE). Also re-confirmed with a second independent sighting: `AlterTableAddCheck` propagates only to `PartitionChildren`, never `InheritanceChildren` (M0134-0005ac row).
  - [x] **M0134-0005aq — the partition walk that stopped one level down** — **LANDED 2026-08-19.** Discharges the deferral row 0005ap filed the same day and is the campaign's third **DML** correctness fix. On a sub-partitioned table (root → intermediate partition that is itself `PARTITION BY` → leaf), **all four** DML forms reported `0` rows and left the leaf untouched, with no error: `UPDATE root_p SET …`, `DELETE FROM root_p`, `UPDATE root_p … FROM other`, `DELETE FROM root_p USING other` — each `1` on PG 18.3, live-verified side by side. `SELECT` saw the rows the whole time, which is what kept the gap invisible. **Root cause:** `catalog.InMemory.PartitionChildren` (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:4510`) returns direct children only, and all four expansion sites in `internal/executor/operators_storage.go` called it raw, so the fan-out list held the storage-less intermediate node and never the leaf. The hierarchy's other two consumers had each already solved this independently — INSERT routing via `routeToPartitionDepth` (`:3014`) and the read path via `collectAllPartitionLeaves` (`internal/optimizer/planner.go:3350`) — leaving DML the last flat consumer. **Upstream cannot express it:** expansion is ONE site, `expand_inherited_rtentry` (`postgres/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c:86`), and it recurses; the **sixth** consecutive instance of this campaign's shape. Fix is +42 lines, one file: new `collectDMLPartitionLeaves` (`:2869`) — BFS, **partitions-only** (inheritance children stay a separate branch per site), **leaves-only** (a node with a non-empty `PartitionKey` is recursed into, never scanned, since intermediate nodes have no storage and must not be heap-locked), `seen` cycle guard — swapped in at all four sites (`updateOp.Next:5166`, `deleteOp.Next:6204`, `updateOp.updateWithFrom:6655`, `deleteOp.deleteWithUsing:7180`) with the `!o.plan.Only` gate, the `colMap: nil` partition split and the per-child `RowExclusiveLock` all untouched. **`allDescendants` (`operators_fk.go:1004`) was deliberately NOT reused** — it mixes in inheritance children, returns non-leaf nodes, and filters on `transam.CurrentPartitionDetachEpoch()`, a globally-current epoch that is intentionally FK/RI-specific (`operators_fk.go:1036-1049`); the new helper filters on the statement's own `ctx.Snap.PartitionDetachEpoch` via `catalog.VisiblePartitionChildren`, mirroring `:3008`. Side effect worth naming: the four DML sites previously applied **no** detach-visibility filter at all, so a concurrently detached partition is now correctly excluded from the fan-out too. Guards: `internal/executor/operators_dml_subpartition_test.go` (new, 6 tests) — one per broken form asserting both the count and the **leaf table queried by its own name**, plus a one-level regression guard and an `UPDATE ONLY` fan-out-suppression guard; FAIL-pre proven by stashing only the source file (all four reported `RowsAffected=0`, leaf unchanged). Putting the loop INSIDE the existing `if` rather than a new one is what keeps `DELETE FROM ONLY <partitioned_parent> USING …` a no-op. The EPQ retry loop (`:7248+`) needed no change: it is generic over `victim{rel,blk,slot,cols}` and `epqSlotMovedToAnotherPartition` (`:7321`) keys off `vRel`/`v.blk`/`v.slot`, so a partition-sourced victim — including one moved to a sibling partition under RC — flows through unmodified, as `deleteOp.Next` already proved. PG emits both spellings and the CALLER picks: `ruleutils.c:pg_oper_expr` (~:10735-10769) self-wraps every `OpExpr` only when `!PRETTY_PAREN`, psql `\d+` always passes `pretty=true` (`src/bin/psql/describe.c:2530`), pg_dump passes `false`/the 1-arg form (`pg_dump.c:7768`, `ruleutils.c:2152`). goopg's dispatch arm (`internal/executor/expr.go`) never read the argument, so every consumer got the non-pretty form.   - [x] **M0134-0005ag — `pg_get_partition_constraintdef` builtin (bucket D)** — **LANDED 2026-08-19.** The function was seeded in pg_proc (OID 3408, `internal/initdb/pg_proc_seed_data.go:2272`) but had **no executor implementation**, so psql `\d+` failed outright on EVERY partition with `ERROR: function pg_catalog.pg_get_partition_constraintdef does not exist` — regress hunk #13 (31 lines), but the real blast radius was all partition introspection. goopg already stores fully *parsed* partition metadata (`catalog.PartitionBound` `catalog.go:1510-1554`, `PartitionParentOf` `:4563`), so the fix is one dispatch arm in `internal/executor/expr.go` modelled on `pg_get_constraintdef` plus four local render helpers. Two PG facts drove it: `pg_get_partition_constraintdef` returns SQL **NULL, not an error**, for a non-partition or empty qual (`partcache.c:299 get_partition_qual_relid`), and it deparses with `PRETTYFLAG_INDENT` **without** `PRETTYFLAG_PAREN`, so AND/OR add an outer paren pair on top of each self-parenthesizing arm — hence the expected `((a IS NOT NULL) AND (a = 1))`. The research report's claim that PG's `T_NullTest` does *not* self-parenthesize was **wrong** (`ruleutils.c:10224` — it does); the implementation used a local builder rather than `defaultExprToSQL`, so `operators_ddl.go` has **zero diff lines** and the `renderCheckPredicate` / index-predicate siblings are unaffected by construction. Covered: single-level column-key LIST (single value, multi-value `= ANY (ARRAY[…])`, NULL-accepting), single-column RANGE, HASH. DEFAULT partitions, multi-level, multi-column RANGE and expression keys return NULL and are **ledgered** rather than rendered wrong (a plausible-but-wrong qual would be a silent-wrong-answer bug). Design: `docs/design/0134-0005ag-partition-constraintdef.md`. Measurement: constraints **294 lines / 14 hunks -> 290 / 15**; the +1 hunk is a diff **context-split**, verified by the coordinator, not a regression — `Partition constraint: ((a IS NOT NULL) AND (a = 1))` is now a matching CONTEXT line and the residue in that window is two pre-existing unrelated gaps (`CHECK ((a > 0))` vs PG's `CHECK (a > 0)`; missing `(inherited)` tag on inherited NOT NULL), both newly ledgered.
